messages.subject: Displaying Covariate Effects from Inlabru
parts:
Hi all,

I'm trying to display the effects of my inlabru model covariates in a format that is more easily understood. From what I have seen in MCMC forums, the covariates and their relative effects can be displayed as a series of horizontal bars representing 95% credible intervals below, rather than a series of Gaussian curves, with posterior distribution functions on the y axis. 

Does anyone know how to display the covariates of an inlabru model in this format? (Image attached below).

Thanks for your help.
Sol

Hi,

If you extract the quantiles from the inla output ($summary.fixed has them for fixed effects) this should just be a matter of choosing a suitable geom_ in ggplot. I haven’t made that specific type of plot with ggplot, but that’s where I’d look for solutions.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Displaying Covariate Effects from Inlabru
parts:
Hi Finn,

This did the trick! Thanks for your help Finn.

Here's the dot-plot code for anyone who comes across this subject in the future:

nc.cov <- ggplot(nest.model, aes(y=mean, ymin=q1, ymax=q3, x= Cov))+
  geom_pointrange()+
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype=2)+
  coord_flip()+
  geom_point(size=3, colour="#FF9900")+
  theme_classic()+
  xlab('Variable')
nc.cov

Cheers,
Sol
